title: How Many Counterfactuals Does It Take? Probing VLM Hallucinations Through Circuits and Causal Effects
abstract: arXiv:2606.08777v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Visual Language Models (VLMs) are known to produce hallucinated predictions that are not grounded in visual evidence, yet existing approaches lack a principled understanding of how robust such predictions are under counterfactual perturbations. In this work, we study the sample complexity of counterfactual robustness for hallucinated outputs in VLMs. We define a causal influence metric based on log-probability differences between factual, counterfactual, and activation-patched runs, and use it to characterize the stability of hallucinated predictions. By leveraging circuit discovery techniques (CD-T), we identify model components responsible for these predictions and track their activation differences across counterfactual samples. translated_title: 需要多少个反事实样本？通过电路与因果效应探究视觉语言模型的幻觉现象
translated_abstract: 视觉语言模型已知会产生不基于视觉证据的幻觉预测，然而现有方法缺乏对这些预测在反事实扰动下鲁棒性的原理性理解。在这项工作中，我们研究了视觉语言模型中幻觉输出的反事实鲁棒性的样本复杂度。我们定义了一个基于事实、反事实和激活修补运行之间对数概率差异的因果影响度量，并用它来表征幻觉预测的稳定性。通过利用电路发现技术，我们识别出负责这些幻觉预测的模型组件，并跟踪它们在不同反事实样本间的激活差异。随后，我们利用集中不等式和方差估计，推导出可靠检测幻觉输出不稳定性所需的最小反事实样本数的经验界限。
tldr: 该论文提出基于对数概率差异的因果影响度量并结合电路发现技术，量化了视觉语言模型幻觉输出的反事实鲁棒性，并推导出可靠检测幻觉不稳定性所需最小反事实样本数的经验界限。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a causal influence metric based on log-probability differences combined with circuit discovery techniques to quantify the counterfactual robustness of VLM hallucinations, and derives empirical bounds on the minimum number of counterfactual samples required to reliably detect instability in hallucinated outputs.
